findings.title: Task 3.1 makes `world_bounds` required, which breaks existing callers and may be invalid syntax
findings.description:
Task 3.1 (lines 186–191) adds a "new required keyword argument `world_bounds`" to `SimulationManager.__init__`.
- It gives no position for the parameter. The signature already ends with defaulted parameters, and Python rejects a required parameter after a defaulted one unless it is keyword-only. Putting it before `environment` breaks positional callers instead.
- The current code has `world_bounds: WorldBoundsConfig | None = None`, falling back to `entity_manager.world_bounds`. That is a different, softer contract than the plan describes. The slice design (line 272) also says "required".
- About 20 existing `SimulationManager(...)` calls in `tests/test_simulation.py` (lines 137–565) omit `world_bounds`. So do `tests/test_force_builder.py:201` and `tests/test_repulsor_integration.py:53`.
- Task 3.4 tells the implementer to patch the `test_simulation.py` calls. Task 3.5 names `test_force_builder.py` and `test_clients.py`. `test_clients.py` constructs no `SimulationManager`, and `test_repulsor_integration.py` is missing from the list.
- Pick one contract: required keyword-only with the full call-site list, or optional with the entity-manager fallback. Either removes the churn.

findings.title: Task 3.4 reflect-flip test cannot pass with the fixture parameters the repo uses
findings.description:
Line 231 places an agent at `(99, 50)` with velocity `(10, 0)` and steps once, expecting `vx < 0`.
- `tick` runs `integrate`, which clamps velocity to the profile `max_speed` (`src/migratory/engine/integration.py:43`). The existing `_profile()` helper and `profile_configs_dict` use `max_speed=5.0`.
- Existing tests use `dt=0.05`. The agent therefore moves to about 99.25, never crosses 100, and nothing reflects.
- The task states neither `dt` nor `max_speed`. The 50-step open, wrap and reflect tests (lines 228–230) have the same gap: an outward start velocity may not push 4 agents out of a 100×100 world in 50 steps at 5 units/s and `dt=0.05`.
- Specify `dt`, `max_speed` and start positions that guarantee a crossing, or the junior implementer will hit failing tests with no guidance.

findings.title: Plan states wrong line numbers and a stale three-variant enum and file state
findings.description:
- Task 1.1 says `WorldBoundsConfig` is at line 25. It is at line 47.
- Task 1.3 says `_validate_world_bounds()` is around line 156. It is at line 180.
- Task 1.2 says `policy` is "the third field (after `height`)". `soft_bounds` now follows it.
- Task 2.1 says the `match` has "three variants", and the parametrized dispatch test in 2.3 covers "all three policies". `BoundsPolicy.SOFT` now exists, and `apply_bounds_policy` has a `SOFT` case (`bounds_enforcement.py:41`).
- Note line 332 says `SOFT` is "intentionally deferred", which is no longer true (CHANGELOG line 15 records slice 314).
- Task 1.3's `return WorldBoundsConfig(...)` call now also passes `soft_bounds`.
- The tasks and tests described here already exist in the repo, while every checkbox is `[ ]` and the frontmatter says `status: complete`. The status and checklist contradict each other.

findings.title: Wrap implementation can return exactly `width`, violating success criterion 7, and no test covers it
findings.description:
Task 2.2 (lines 130–134) relies on `np.mod(x, width)` producing values in `[0, width)`.
- For a tiny negative overshoot such as `-1e-17`, floating-point `np.mod` returns exactly `width`, so the result is outside the half-open interval.
- Success criterion 7 requires `[0, width)`.
- Task 3.4's `test_wrap_policy_keeps_all_positions_inside` asserts `x < width`, so it could fail intermittently.
- Task 2.3 has no tiny-negative-overshoot case and Task 2.2 has no guard.
- Add a case and a step to fold `== width` back to 0.

findings.title: Round-trip test is weaker than success criterion 5
findings.description: Criterion 5 requires that reloading the emitted YAML "produces an equal `ServerConfig`". Task 1.4 (line 88) asserts only that the policy matches. The existing `TestConfigToYaml` (line 782) compares the whole `world_bounds`. Change the assertion to full `ServerConfig` equality.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox tasks, and there are more than a 2/5 slice needs
findings.description:
Tasks 1.5, 2.4, 3.6, 4.3 and 5.5 are separate numbered tasks whose commit lines are checkboxes (`- [ ] **Commit:**`). Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checkboxes. Five commits for a two-file config change plus one small module is too many.
- Task 4.3 commits two one-line YAML edits on their own.
- Tasks 4.1 and 4.2 are two near-identical tasks that should merge, and could fold into Section 3.
- Fold the commits into plain marker lines after Sections 1–3 and the final docs step.

findings.title: Redundant and low-value verification and test tasks
findings.description:
- The full `pytest` suite runs in 3.5, 5.1 and again as 5.2 step 2.
- The parametrized "dispatches correctly and does not raise" test (line 171) duplicates the per-policy tests above it and asserts nothing the criteria need.
- `test_open_is_noop_positions` and `test_open_is_noop_velocities` could be one test.
- Drop 5.1, drop or merge the redundant tests, and merge 4.1 and 4.2.

findings.title: Manual walkthrough edits a tracked config in place and leaves no recovery path
findings.description:
Task 5.2 steps 6–7 (lines 304–306) change `policy:` in the tracked `config/test.yaml` to `reflect`, then `open`. The only undo is step 8, a manual restore.
- If the run stops after step 6 or 7, `test.yaml` stays on `reflect` or `open`. The Task 5.5 `git add` of "all updated docs" could pick it up, and the slice's own criterion 12 requires `wrap` there.
- Use temporary copies of the config, for example `--config /tmp/...`, so the shipped file is never modified.
- Step 4 and the slice's step 4 also say "Spawned 100 entities", but `test.yaml` spawns 160 (150 + 10).

findings.title: Task 3.2 and the Notes contradict each other on import overhead
findings.description: Task 3.2 asks the implementer to confirm "zero import-time ... overhead", but the same task adds a module-level `import apply_bounds_policy` in `simulation.py`. Line 329 says "No import of `apply_bounds_policy` is avoided". Remove the import-time claim. Say only that the `OPEN` path performs no call and no array slicing.

findings.title: Task 5.3 and Task 3.5 contain unverifiable or already-done references
findings.description:
- Line 241 refers to "slice 309's Task 3.2" fix pattern. That cannot be checked from this file.
- Task 5.3 sets `status: complete` in both documents, but both already say `complete`.
- Line 314 asks to tick the `(313)` line in `300-slices.worldserver-foundation.md`. The long matching lines (43, 45) were not displayed, so whether it is already checked is unconfirmed.
- Task 5.4's CHANGELOG entries already exist (CHANGELOG lines 27, 28, 42). The task would duplicate them. Reword it to "verify or amend".

findings.title: Success criterion coverage map
findings.description:
- Criteria 1–2 map to Tasks 1.1, 1.2. Criteria 3–4 map to 1.3, 1.4. Criterion 5 maps to 1.4, only partially (see above). Criteria 6–9 map to 2.1–2.3.
- Criterion 10 maps to 3.2 and 3.4. Criterion 11 maps to 3.4. Criterion 12 maps to 4.1, 4.2. Criterion 13 maps to 3.5. Criterion 14 maps to 5.2.
- The log line in 3.3 traces to walkthrough step 4.
- The slice states no NFRs, so no load test or CI gating task is required.
